note: Hour-by-hour account of the 'Sansad Chalo' march, compiled 2026-11-12 for Vali's review. Sources: the dossier (Claude.pdf pp1, 6, 13, 15, 19, 21; it has no clock times for 20 Jul) plus public, non-paywalled outlets, mainly the Tribune and ThePrint live blogs, ThePrint's 'top 10 developments', PTI copy, Newslaundry, Outlook, The Caravan, The South First, Deccan Chronicle and Wikipedia. Rule: primary source wins; paywalled pages excluded. Times are IST as displayed; live-blog stamps are posting times, so an event may be earlier than its stamp. Map positions: 'approx' = from OSM or known geography; 'illustrative' = no source gives the position. Crowd shares are illustrative only. fact_ref indexes summary_facts within the same step. 'in_ledger' names the existing ledger fact (null = new). Snippets marked 'summarising fetch' were read through a summarising web tool; check them on the page before quoting.

open_questions: First baton charge: ThePrint says 7.30 am near Park Hotel; the Tribune live blog's first lathi-charge entry is 10:37 am; Delhi Police denied any violence at 11:07 am and 3.29 pm. All three can be true (separate incidents), but no source reconciles them.
Dipke's 'detention': Das claimed it at 2:47 pm (ThePrint 2.56 pm) and retracted it at 3:38–3:55 pm; The South First says Dipke and Dimple Yadav were detained and released later in the day.

Detention count over the day: 'more than 20' (officials, PTI, 4:45 pm) → 'more than 100' (police sources, PTI, 8:25 pm) → 'about 70' (Delhi Police statement, 11:54 pm) → later police denial (dossier p19/p21, not re-checked). CJP also cited ~70 (Wikipedia).

RML: ~100 by 5.30 pm incl. 10 police (Newslaundry citing IE); 65 MLCs by 7 pm (Wikipedia, hospital and police sources); 'more than 200' brought to emergency by late evening (Tribune). The Tribune figure is new and larger; its source is unclear.

Crowd: CJP 'one lakh' (7.20 am); 'over fifty thousand' (Caravan reporters); 'tens of thousands' (Guardian); 'more than 10,000' (DCP via Al Jazeera); 'close to 1,000' reached near Parliament (South First). The last is a sub-group, not the total.
Section 163 BNSS: PTI says police 'imposed' it 'at around 1 pm'; DCP Sharma and the 19–20 July reports say it was already in force. Possibly a fresh order for a wider area; unresolved.
Barricade height: '8-foot' (ThePrint), 'some over six feet tall' (Newslaundry), 'seven-foot' (CPI's D Raja). Show no number, or show each with its claimant.

Pellets: 2 rounds (police GD via Tribune) vs 7 rounds, 5 hits (CRPF report via The Wire). Newslaundry places 3 pellet victims at or near Palika Bazar at about 3, 4 and 5 pm, and an RAF shotgun video at the Regal complex. No source gives the firing positions.
Who fired: ANI says 'RPF' (Railway Protection Force); the Tribune, the GD and Newslaundry say RAF. Probably an ANI error, but keep as quoted.
Raisina Road roundabout (ThePrint) is not identified; it may be the Windsor Place end or the Rail Bhawan end. Placed illustratively at the Windsor Place end.

No source gives barricade coordinates. Named barricade points: Jantar Mantar entrance (both sides), Tolstoy Marg, Parliament Street/high-security zone, SBI building on Sansad Marg, Constitution Club, Press Club, near Parliament, Shankar Road (PTI list), Shastri Bhawan, Rail Bhawan, Janpath (Dynamite News). Lines on the map stay 'illustrative'.

No hour-by-hour police strength exists in any source. Only day totals (5,000+; 32 companies + 14 district contingents; 25+ CAPF battalions) and 300+ at the site at 7 am. The map should show the totals once, not per step.

Internet: no source gives a start time (earliest mention 9:23 am, Tribune) or an exact end ('until the evening', The Week). Area: 'parts of Central Delhi, including the area around Jantar Mantar' (IFF). South First's '5-km radius' and jammers are single-source.
Mandi House lathi charge (PTI eyewitnesses) has no time; DT Next's '5:23 am' stamp may be UTC.

Blocked or not fetched: Hindustan Times, Times of India, News18, Business Standard and Deccan Herald (403 or blocked); The Wire's pellet article body (headline only); Indian Express (paywall policy). Their details are used only where relayed by another outlet.
Several snippets come from a summarising fetch tool, not a raw page read. Those carry a note; re-check wording on the page before quoting on screen.
